chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from al-Ays said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the synagogues and the churches, 'Is it correct to break these two in order to build the Masjids?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to demolish churches and synagogues to build mosques in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the peribility of dismantling synagogues and churches to build mosques, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view on the repurposing of non-Muslim places of worship. This ruling is often contextualized within the broader principle of Islamic sovereignty and the elevation of the word of God, as discussed by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi. The hadith underscores the practical application of territorial conquest and religious dominance in early Islamic history.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan, from Al Ays who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the synagogues and the churches, ‘Is it correct to break these two in order to build the Masjids?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from al-‘Is who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Biya‘ and churches if they can be changed into Masjid. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is possible.’”
